teams.heading: Fiji chase first Nations Championship points after third consecutive defeat in Scotland
teams.body: Fiji go into the weekend sitting twelfth on the 12-team log after failing to secure a victory in their first three Nations Championship fixtures. The Flying Fijians lost 17-33 to Scotland in the third round, leaving them with only 49 points scored in the tournament. The squad have also conceded 145 points across those three opening matches. Fiji will face France next, aiming to improve on the 34-21 away defeat they suffered against the French team during an international friendly in November 2025.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje praises Steve Borthwick’s surprise sabbatical decision after summer rest
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje has defended his decision to skip the July Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, admitting the surprise proposal from head coach Steve Borthwick caught him off guard. Having breached player-load thresholds after a demanding year on and off the field, the 31-year-old lock sat out the Nations Championship tour for a much-needed mental and physical break. "I don't regret it at all," Itoje said, believing the proactive rest will help him "come back better" for club and country this season.

teams.heading: George Skivington rules out Ross Byrne move to Munster after Crowley injury
teams.body: Gloucester head coach George Skivington has dismissed suggestions that fly-half Ross Byrne could return to Ireland with Munster. Speculation linked the 31-year-old with a move to Limerick following the news that Jack Crowley is sidelined with a vascular injury until the new year. Despite Byrne slipping down the Kingsholm pecking order last season, Skivington confirmed the playmaker is central to his plans. "Ross is still with us," Skivington insisted, adding that Gloucester's packed schedule across three tournaments will provide ample opportunities.

teams.heading: Luciano Avaca scores hat-trick as Argentina XV crush Uruguay XV 58-10
teams.body: The Argentina XV took another giant step in the Americas Rugby Championship on Wednesday, routing a suspension-hit Uruguay XV 58-10 in their second-round clash. Luciano Avaca stole the show with a brilliant hat-trick, while fullback Franco Rossetto also crossed twice to secure a 10-try bonus-point victory. Led by captain Rodrigo Fernández Criado, the selection showed clinical improvement following their opening win over Paraguay. The side now prepares for a final-round decider against Chile.

teams.heading: James O'Connor rejoins Western Force to launch late Wallabies World Cup bid
teams.body: Veteran playmaker James O'Connor has rejoined the Western Force for the 2027 season, launching a late bid to force his way back into national contention ahead of next year's home World Cup. The 36-year-old utility back, who has 68 caps, returns to Perth after a stint with Leicester Tigers. O'Connor hopes the move will capture the attention of head coach Les Kiss. "He knows I'm hungry for it. He knows I want to be involved. So I'll let my rugby do the talking," O'Connor said.

teams.heading: Timothy Lafaele and Brave Blossoms stars win league eligibility legal battle
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has reached a court settlement to reverse proposed eligibility restrictions that targeted foreign-born naturalised players. A group of 24 players, including Brave Blossoms internationals Timothy Lafaele and Jiwon Gu, filed for a provisional injunction against rules that would have limited their matchday involvement. Under the revised criteria, naturalised citizens who held citizenship by May 2025 will be treated as native-born players. The league admitted "prior explanations and communication with all relevant parties were insufficient" and will reclassify all players with 30 or more caps.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie rotates All Blacks pack as Codie Taylor misses Soweto Test
teams.body: New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie has overhauled his forward pack for Saturday’s third Test against South Africa, resting vice-captain Codie Taylor. Asafo Aumua starts at hooker while Peter Lakai and Sam Darry earn promotions to the starting fifteen, replacing Simon Parker and Fabian Holland. As lock Tupou Vaa'i prepares for his 50th Test, the series remains locked at 1-1. A victory in Soweto would see the All Blacks reclaim the world No. 1 ranking and trigger a third consecutive week of changes at the summit.

lead.why: The significant pack rotation and omission of Codie Taylor for the third Test is the day's primary talking point.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus moves Cheslin Kolbe to full-back for New Zealand Test
teams.body: Cheslin Kolbe will start at full-back in Saturday’s third Test against New Zealand at FNB Stadium, a tactical shift intended to counter the All Blacks' expansive game. With Kolbe moving to No. 15, Ethan Hooker earns a start on the wing alongside Kurt-Lee Arendse, who makes his 34th appearance. Arendse dismissed concerns over the reshuffled backline, insisting the "tools are pretty much the same" as the world champions look to build momentum in Soweto following Kolbe’s 18-point performance during the 33-26 victory in Cape Town.
